three_node_execution.reason: llama.cpp CUDA build still compiling on HOST-B and HOST-C (90% / 125%). rpc-server built and verified on HOST-A.

distributed_attempt.setup: llama.cpp llama-cli on HOST-A + ggml-rpc-server on HOST-B and HOST-C, port 10200 (mapped)
distributed_attempt.evidence: HOST-B rpc log: "Accepted client connection"; HOST-C GPU allocated 2452 MiB
distributed_attempt.observation: llama.cpp RPC transfers model tensors to remote devices over the network at load time. HOST-C received 2452 MiB and then stalled at 0% GPU utilisation. Load did not finish within 3 minutes.
distributed_attempt.implication: On A<->B (0.6-1.0 Mbps) the transfer of ~2 GiB per worker would take hours. This is a link-capacity limit, not a code fault.
distributed_attempt.blocked_reason: Weight transfer over the measured links is too slow to finish the load.

conclusion.why: llama.cpp RPC ships weights over TCP at load. The measured WAN links (0.6-1.0 Mbps to B) cannot carry the shards in reasonable time.
what_would_fix_it: Pre-place weights on each worker and use llama.cpp local cache so no transfer is needed
Use a runtime that streams activations only (MESHWEAVE own pipeline) with weights loaded from local disk on each host
conclusion.note: Each host already has the full GGUF locally (6.31 GiB). A design that loads from local disk and only sends activations would avoid the transfer entirely.
